title: Đề luyện Đọc VSTEP A2 — Recall SGU0822 (3 passage)

passages.p1:
Mai and Her First Book

Mai is a young woman from a small town in Vietnam. She is twenty-four years old. She works in a small library during the day. At night, she writes stories. This year, Mai published her first book. The book is called "The Blue Kite." Many people in her town are proud of her.

Mai loved books when she was a child. Her mother read to her every night. Mai listened to many stories about brave girls and kind animals. She wanted to write her own stories one day. When she was ten, she made a small book with paper and crayons. It had only five pages, but she was very happy. She showed it to her mother, and her mother kept it for many years.

"The Blue Kite" is a story about a girl named Lan. Lan is nine years old. She lives with her grandmother near the sea. One day, Lan finds an old blue kite in the garden. The kite is broken, so Lan fixes it. When she flies the kite, she meets a new friend. The friend is a boy who lives next door. Together, they have many small adventures. The book is not long. It has only one hundred pages, and the words are easy. Children can read it alone.

Why did Mai write this book? She says the idea came from her own childhood. When she was young, she had a blue kite too. Her father gave it to her before he moved to another city for work. The kite made her think of him every day. Mai wanted to share this warm feeling with other children. She also wanted to tell them that small things can be important. A simple kite can bring people together.

Writing the book was not easy. Mai worked on it for two years. Some nights she was tired, and the words did not come. Sometimes she wrote ten pages and then threw them away. But she did not stop. Her best friend, Hoa, read every chapter and gave her advice. "Your friend can see the mistakes that you cannot see," Mai says. With Hoa's help, the story slowly became better.

When the book came out, Mai was nervous. She did not know if people would like it. But readers liked it very much. Parents said the story was sweet and easy to understand. Children said Lan felt like a real friend. Some families read one chapter together every evening. One teacher used the book in her class. The students drew pictures of the blue kite and wrote their own short stories. This made Mai very happy. She never thought her small book could do so much.

Now Mai is writing a second book. This one is about a boy and a little dog. She writes a little every day, even when she is busy. She also visits schools sometimes and reads a few pages to the children. They ask her many funny questions, like "Is Lan real?" Mai always smiles and says the story is real in your heart. She keeps her old blue kite on the wall above her desk. When she looks at it, she remembers why she started to write. For Mai, a book is like a gift. You make it with love, and then you give it to someone else. She hopes many children will open her books and smile.
passages.p2:
How Deaf Children Learn Sign Language

Many people know that some children cannot hear. We call them deaf children. What many people do not know is that most deaf children are born to parents who can hear. In fact, more than nine in ten deaf children have hearing parents. These parents love their child very much. But often they do not know any sign language, because they have never needed it before. This is new for the whole family.

Sign language is a real language. People make it with their hands, but they also use their face and body. A smile, a frown, or a raised eyebrow can change the meaning of a sign, just as your voice can change the meaning of a spoken word. Sign language has its own grammar and its own rules. It is not just simple pictures in the air. Deaf people can talk about anything with it — school, food, feelings, jokes, or the news.

Children learn language best when they are very young. A small child's brain is ready to take in a new language quickly and easily. This is true for hearing children who listen to speech, and it is also true for deaf children who watch signs. So it is very important for a deaf child to meet a full sign language early, in the first years of life. When a child learns a language early, it becomes easy and natural, and it stays with the child for many years.

Sometimes a hearing family cannot find sign language classes near their home. They still want to talk with their child, so they make up their own signs at home. These are often called home signs. Home signs can help a little. A child and parents can point, act things out, and agree on a few signs for common things like milk, sleep, or outside. This is better than nothing, and it shows the family's love.

But home signs are small. They only work inside one house, with a few people. A shared sign language is much better. A shared sign language is used by many people in many places. When a child learns it, the child can talk with teachers, with other deaf children, and with deaf adults. The child can learn new words all the time and can join a bigger group of friends. Home signs cannot grow this way, because only the family knows them.

For this reason, many people who study language say the same thing. Deaf children should learn a full, shared sign language as soon as they can. They can still learn to read, and some can learn to speak too. But a strong first language gives them a good start for everything else, like reading, school, and making friends.

There is good news for hearing parents. They do not have to be perfect signers on the first day. They can learn sign language together with their child, step by step. Many towns have classes, videos, and deaf clubs where families can meet deaf adults and practice. Deaf adults can be kind guides and show the child what is possible in life.

So the main idea is simple. Deaf children need a real language early, and a shared sign language gives them the most. With help, love, and a little time, a deaf child and a hearing family can share a full language and a happy life together.
passages.p3:
Young People and Social Media Apps

Many years ago, Facebook was the most popular app for young people. Almost everyone had an account. Students used it to talk with friends, share photos, and read the news. But things are different now. Today, many young people do not use Facebook very much. They still have an account, but they open it only a few times each week. Some of them almost never look at it.

So who uses Facebook now? The answer may surprise you. In many families, it is the parents and the grandparents who use Facebook the most. Older people like it because it is easy. They can see family photos, send birthday messages, and join groups about cooking, gardening, or their old school. For them, Facebook is a nice and simple place. When young people see their mother, father, or grandmother on Facebook, some of them feel that the app is not really for them anymore.

Young people prefer other apps. Instagram and Snapchat are two big favourites. On Instagram, users post photos and short videos. They can follow singers, football players, and friends, and they can watch fun clips for hours. Snapchat is a little different. On Snapchat, a photo or message often disappears after a short time. Because of this, some young people feel that Snapchat is more private. They can send a silly picture to a close friend and not worry that everyone will see it later.

There are a few reasons why these newer apps are so popular. First, they are fun. They are full of photos, music, and short videos, so there is always something new to look at. Second, they feel more private. On Facebook, a post can be seen by the whole family, including aunts, uncles, and old teachers. On Snapchat or Instagram, many young people share things only with a small group of close friends. This feels safer and more relaxed. Third, these apps are made for phones. Young people usually do not use a computer for social media. They use their phone all day, and Instagram and Snapchat are quick and easy on a small screen. A young person can open an app, watch a video, and reply to a friend in just a few seconds, even while walking to school or waiting for a bus.

However, we should not say that Facebook is dead. That is not true. Facebook is still one of the biggest apps in the world. Billions of people still open it every month, and many companies use it to sell things and talk to customers. In some countries, Facebook is still very strong, even among young people. So the app has not disappeared. It has simply changed. It is now more popular with older users than with teenagers and students.

What will happen in the future? Nobody knows for sure. Apps come and go. Ten years ago, few people knew about Snapchat, and now it is everywhere. Maybe in ten years there will be a new app that everyone loves, and Instagram and Snapchat will feel old, just like Facebook does to many young people today. One thing seems clear: young people always want something fresh, fun, and a little bit private. They want a space that feels like their own, away from their parents. For now, that space is not Facebook. It is the newer apps on their phones, where they share photos and videos with the friends they care about the most.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

What is the passage mainly about?
options: A. A famous old library in a big city in Vietnam
B. A young woman who wrote her own first storybook
C. A boy who flies a blue kite beside the sea
D. How to make a small paper book with crayons
questions.explanation: Bài đọc xoay quanh Mai và việc cô cho ra đời cuốn sách đầu tay của mình; các đáp án còn lại chỉ là chi tiết phụ hoặc nhân vật trong truyện.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

How old is Mai?
options: A. She is nine years old.
B. She is ten years old.
C. She is twenty years old.
D. She is now twenty-four.
questions.explanation: Bài đọc nói rõ Mai hai mươi bốn tuổi; số chín và mười là tuổi của Lan và tuổi lúc Mai làm cuốn sách nhỏ đầu tiên.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

Who is the main character in "The Blue Kite"?
options: A. A young girl called Lan who lives near the sea
B. A boy who lives in the house next door
C. Mai's best friend, whose name is Hoa
D. Mai's father, who works in another city
questions.explanation: Câu chuyện kể về cô bé Lan sống cùng bà gần biển; cậu bé hàng xóm chỉ là bạn của Lan, còn Hoa và bố Mai không thuộc nội dung sách.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

In paragraph 6, the word "nervous" is closest in meaning to...
options: A. very proud and completely sure
B. very angry and quite upset
C. a little worried and unsure
D. very tired and rather sleepy
questions.explanation: Ngay sau đó bài đọc nói Mai không biết mọi người có thích sách không, cho thấy "nervous" mang nghĩa lo lắng, chưa yên tâm.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

In "The kite made her think of him every day," the word "him" refers to...
options: A. the boy who lives next door
B. Mai's father
C. her best friend, Hoa
D. a teacher at a school
questions.explanation: Câu trước đó cho biết bố tặng Mai cánh diều rồi chuyển đi xa, nên "him" chính là người bố mà Mai nhớ mỗi ngày.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

Who gave Mai her own blue kite?
options: A. Her father, before he left for another city
B. Her mother, who read to her at night
C. Her best friend, whose name is Hoa
D. A teacher who once used her book
questions.explanation: Bài đọc nói rõ bố tặng Mai cánh diều trước khi ông chuyển đi làm ở nơi khác; mẹ chỉ đọc sách, còn Hoa và cô giáo không liên quan đến cánh diều.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

Which of the following is NOT true about the book "The Blue Kite"?
options: A. It is about one hundred pages long.
B. The language in it is simple to read.
C. Children are able to read it on their own.
D. Mai finished writing it in just a few weeks.
questions.explanation: Bài đọc cho biết Mai mất tới hai năm để viết, nên ý "chỉ vài tuần" là sai; ba ý còn lại đều đúng với mô tả về cuốn sách.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

Why does Mai keep the old blue kite above her desk?
options: A. Because she plans to sell it one day
B. Because it was a present from her friend
C. Because it reminds her why she began writing
D. Because she uses it to teach the children
questions.explanation: Bài đọc nói khi nhìn cánh diều, Mai nhớ lý do mình bắt đầu viết; đó là ý nghĩa tinh thần, không phải để bán hay để dạy học.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

Who read every chapter and helped Mai make the story better?
options: A. Her close friend, Hoa, who gave advice
B. Her mother, who read the whole book
C. A teacher at a school in her town
D. The boy who lives right next door
questions.explanation: Bài đọc nói rõ bạn thân Hoa đọc mọi chương và góp ý, nhờ đó câu chuyện tốt hơn; mẹ và cô giáo không làm việc này.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

How does Mai feel about writing a book?
options: A. She thinks it is a rather boring job.
B. She thinks it is mainly about earning money.
C. She thinks it is too hard to enjoy.
D. She thinks it is a caring gift she makes for others.
questions.explanation: Ở cuối bài, Mai ví cuốn sách như một món quà được làm bằng tình yêu rồi trao cho người khác, cho thấy thái độ trân trọng và yêu thích.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A. Most parents of deaf children are also deaf.
B. Sign language is too hard for young children to learn.
C. Deaf children benefit from learning a full, common sign language when young.
D. Home signs are all a deaf child really needs.
questions.explanation: Toàn bài, đặc biệt đoạn cuối, nhấn mạnh trẻ điếc cần một ngôn ngữ thật sự từ sớm và ngôn ngữ ký hiệu dùng chung mang lại nhiều nhất.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

According to the passage, most deaf children have parents who...
options: A. can hear and often do not know sign language.
B. are deaf and use sign language at home.
C. can hear and are already expert signers.
D. learned sign language before the child was born.
questions.explanation: Bài nói hầu hết trẻ điếc sinh ra từ cha mẹ nghe được, và những cha mẹ này thường chưa biết ngôn ngữ ký hiệu vì trước đây chưa cần.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

The passage says a person's face is important in sign language because...
options: A. it makes the signs faster to read.
B. faces are easier than hands to copy.
C. signs are just simple pictures in the air.
D. a facial expression can change what a sign means.
questions.explanation: Bài viết một nụ cười, cái cau mày hay nhướng mày có thể thay đổi ý nghĩa của một ký hiệu, giống như giọng nói làm với từ.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

In the passage, what are "home signs"?
options: A. Signs that are taught in special language classes.
B. Signs a family invents on its own to use together.
C. Signs that all deaf people everywhere use.
D. Signs that are shown only in videos and clubs.
questions.explanation: Ký hiệu nhà là các ký hiệu do chính gia đình tự tạo ra ở nhà khi không tìm được lớp học gần đó.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

Why is it easier for a very young child to learn a language?
options: A. A young child's brain can pick up a new language fast.
B. Young children have more free time to practise.
C. Young children already know some signs.
D. Young children do not need any help at all.
questions.explanation: Bài nói bộ não của một em bé nhỏ sẵn sàng tiếp nhận ngôn ngữ mới nhanh và dễ, đúng cho cả trẻ nghe được lẫn trẻ điếc.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

In the sentence "because only the family knows them," the word "them" refers to...
options: A. the deaf children.
B. the many places.
C. the teachers and friends.
D. the home signs.
questions.explanation: Câu nói ký hiệu nhà không thể lớn lên vì chỉ gia đình biết "chúng", nên "chúng" chính là các ký hiệu nhà.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

According to the passage, a shared sign language is better than home signs because...
options: A. it is quicker to learn than home signs.
B. it lets the child talk with many more people.
C. it does not use the face or the body.
D. it is used only inside the family home.
questions.explanation: Ngôn ngữ dùng chung được nhiều người ở nhiều nơi dùng, nên em bé có thể trò chuyện với thầy cô, trẻ điếc khác và người lớn bị điếc.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

The passage mentions ALL of the following as true about sign language EXCEPT:
options: A. It has its own grammar and rules.
B. People use their hands, face, and body.
C. It can only be understood by the child's own family.
D. Deaf people can use it to talk about many topics.
questions.explanation: Chỉ gia đình mới hiểu là đặc điểm của ký hiệu nhà, không phải của ngôn ngữ ký hiệu; bài nói người điếc dùng nó để nói về mọi thứ.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

What can we understand about hearing parents from the passage?
options: A. They should not sign until they are perfect.
B. They cannot learn sign language at their age.
C. They must send the child away to a special school.
D. They can pick up signing step by step as their child learns too.
questions.explanation: Bài nói cha mẹ không cần hoàn hảo ngay ngày đầu và có thể học cùng con từng bước, nên họ học dần dần bên cạnh con.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

According to the passage, where can families meet deaf adults?
options: A. Only inside the family's own home.
B. At deaf clubs and classes held in many towns.
C. At the child's future place of work.
D. Almost nowhere close to where they live.
questions.explanation: Bài nói nhiều thị trấn có lớp học, video và câu lạc bộ người điếc, nơi các gia đình gặp gỡ và luyện tập với người lớn bị điếc.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A. Facebook has closed and no one can use it now.
B. Many young people have moved to newer apps, while older people now use Facebook more.
C. Parents should not be allowed to make a Facebook account.
D. Instagram and Snapchat are the only apps left in the world.
questions.explanation: Bài đọc nói người trẻ chuyển sang app mới còn cha mẹ, ông bà dùng Facebook nhiều nhất. Đó là ý xuyên suốt cả bài.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

According to the passage, who uses Facebook the most in many families now?
options: A. Older family members like parents and grandparents.
B. Small children who cannot read yet.
C. Teenagers who are still in high school.
D. University students who study far from home.
questions.explanation: Bài viết ghi rõ chính cha mẹ và ông bà mới là người dùng Facebook nhiều nhất trong nhiều gia đình.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

Why do some young people feel that Snapchat is more private?
options: A. Because it costs a lot of money to open.
B. Because only teachers are allowed to join it.
C. Because it does not let users post any photos.
D. Because pictures and texts usually disappear soon after being seen.
questions.explanation: Bài đọc giải thích trên Snapchat ảnh và tin nhắn thường biến mất, nên người trẻ thấy nó riêng tư hơn.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

The word "favourites" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to which word?
options: A. problems that people try to avoid
B. rules that people must follow
C. things that people like very much
D. places that are far away
questions.explanation: "Favourites" chỉ những thứ được yêu thích; cả câu nói Instagram và Snapchat là hai cái người trẻ ưa chuộng.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

Which of the following is a reason the passage gives for the popularity of newer apps?
options: A. They work well on phones and are quick to use.
B. They send real letters to your house each day.
C. They only work on large office computers.
D. They ask users to pay a fee every week.
questions.explanation: Bài nêu ba lý do, trong đó có việc các app này được làm cho điện thoại, nhanh và dễ dùng trên màn hình nhỏ.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

In the sentence "Because of this, some young people feel that Snapchat is more private," what does "this" refer to?
options: A. the number of singers on Instagram
B. the fact that photos and messages soon disappear
C. the price of a new mobile phone
D. the groups about cooking and gardening
questions.explanation: "This" trỏ về ý ngay trước: trên Snapchat ảnh hoặc tin nhắn thường mất đi sau ít lâu, nên cảm giác riêng tư hơn.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

According to the passage, all of the following are true about Facebook today EXCEPT:
options: A. Billions of people still open it every month.
B. Companies use it to sell things to customers.
C. It is more popular with older users than with students.
D. It has closed down and no longer exists.
questions.explanation: Bài nói rõ Facebook chưa biến mất, chỉ thay đổi. Vì thế ý "đã đóng cửa, không còn tồn tại" là sai.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

What does the writer say about apps in the future?
options: A. Facebook will surely become the most popular app once again very soon.
B. Snapchat will remain the final social media app for a long time.
C. A new app could become popular and make today’s apps feel old.
D. In the future, young people will give up using phones completely.
questions.explanation: Tác giả đoán có thể mười năm nữa xuất hiện app mới ai cũng thích, làm Instagram và Snapchat trở nên cũ kỹ.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

Why does the writer mention aunts, uncles, and old teachers?
options: A. To show that posts on Facebook may reach relatives young users would rather avoid.
B. To prove that older teachers now make most of the videos posted online.
C. To explain that whole families tend to ignore social media completely.
D. To suggest that the Snapchat app is meant mainly for older relatives.
questions.explanation: Nhắc đến cô, chú, thầy cô cũ để minh họa rằng bài trên Facebook dễ bị cả nhà thấy, nên người trẻ thấy kém riêng tư.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

What do young people seem to want from a social media app, according to the last paragraph?
options: A. An app that their parents and grandparents also use every day.
B. An app that mainly shows news posts from big companies.
C. A cheap app where almost none of their friends are active.
D. A fresh, fun place that feels like theirs, apart from their parents.
questions.explanation: Đoạn cuối nói người trẻ muốn thứ mới mẻ, vui và hơi riêng tư, một không gian như của riêng mình tách khỏi cha mẹ.
